Both GT 3 and Pred 4 identify the same inconsistency: Section 3.2 defines action embeddings as the difference between end and initial state embeddings, but Sections 3.1 and 3.3 do not clarify how this difference embedding integrates with the loss or prediction heads.
GT 4 concerns missing details about hyperparameter tuning for baselines in the Experiments section. None of the findings address this specific experimental design protocol issue.

GT 5 concerns Table 1 lacking variance or confidence intervals for state recognition precision improvements. Pred 2 identifies an arithmetic inconsistency in Table 5, which is a different table and a different type of statistical issue.
GT 6 concerns the Conclusion's omission of ethical considerations, biases, and failure modes. None of the findings address ethical integrity or responsible AI deployment issues.

Both GT 7 and Pred 1 identify the same contradiction: Section 3.1 claims losses are computed on all frames based on ground-truth labels, while Section 3.2 states frame-level annotations are absent and pseudo labels are used, creating inconsistency about supervision granularity.

GT 8 concerns rhetorical manipulation in the Introduction using terms like 'powerful' and 'promising pathway' without tempering expectations. None of the findings address this rhetorical presentation issue.
GT 9 concerns Table 4 showing suspiciously minimal changes when increasing graph concepts from 5 to 15. None of the findings discuss Table 4 or this specific data integrity issue.
GT 10 concerns ambiguity about privileged information (actions/objects) during evaluation in Section 4.1 and Tables 1-2. None of the findings address this experimental design protocol issue.

GT 11 concerns suspicious training time discrepancies in Section 4.1 (8 hours for ChangeIt vs. 30 minutes for HowToChange despite similar dataset sizes). None of the findings address this training time issue.
GT 12 concerns Section 3.1's lack of criteria/thresholds for VLM-based frame filtering. None of the findings address this specific method logic issue about frame filtering.

Both GT 13 and Pred 3 identify issues with the 14.6% improvement claim. GT 13 focuses on overstating generalization to multi-action scenarios, while Pred 3 identifies contradictions between the Introduction's claim and actual results, capturing the same underlying issue of claim distortion.
GT 14 concerns rhetorical exaggeration in the Conclusion about integrating SAGE into vision foundation models. None of the findings address this rhetorical presentation issue in the Conclusion.
